headline: High risk of shared-filesystem conflict and cascading mis-edits; prompt-injection and compliance risks are lower but non-zero.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Both agents can read and write files, so a manual copy-paste or file handoff could carry malicious instructions from one into the other. Kestra’s stdin/stdout and workflow files plus Mentat’s file-based editing create a plausible bridge, but there is no shared MCP or browser channel documented, so the pathway is limited.
conditions: IF an operator copies agent_a output into files or prompts consumed by agent_b
IF agent_b is instructed to treat agent_a-generated text as executable instructions
mitigations: Use a strict prompt delimiter and label agent_a output as untrusted
Review any copied text before feeding it to agent_b
Keep agent_a and agent_b on separate working directories
Disable automatic ingestion of generated files into downstream prompts

B_data_leakage.rationale: Kestra touches logs, inputs, artifacts, database data, cloud storage data, messages, and notifications, while Mentat reads selected source files and sends context to a configured model provider. If they share a workspace, sensitive operational data from agent_a can be exposed through agent_b’s model calls. This is a default-feasible leakage path, not merely unusual configuration.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same filesystem workspace
IF agent_a writes logs, artifacts, or data files that agent_b opens
IF agent_b forwards those files into its model-provider context
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent
Exclude logs and artifacts from agent_b input paths
Redact secrets before agent_b reads files
Run agent_b with a minimal file allowlist
requires-engineering: add workspace isolation or per-agent mounts

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Kestra has broad filesystem write, shell, subprocess, and elevated-privilege requests, while Mentat can write files and modify git state with filesystem-based shared state. In a shared repo or directory, concurrent edits can overwrite each other and corrupt git state; the overlap is dangerous by default because neither profile shows locking or coordination primitives.
conditions: IF both agents target the same directory or git repository
IF agent_a and agent_b run concurrently
IF no external lock serializes writes and git operations
mitigations: Assign disjoint output directories
Serialize write phases with a lock file
Pause one agent before the other edits git state
Commit or snapshot before each agent runs
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: Kestra can generate workflow definitions, logs, and notifications that Mentat may then edit or act on as source files. Mentat’s diff-based workflow can propagate a mistaken upstream artifact into downstream code changes if the operator treats agent_a output as authoritative. The chain exists in default file-based workflows, though not every run will trigger it.
conditions: IF agent_a produces workflow or log content that agent_b uses as input
IF agent_b applies diffs without independent verification
IF the operator accepts agent_b edits derived from agent_a output
mitigations: Require a human review step between agents
Compare agent_b diffs against original sources
Feed agent_b only minimal excerpts from agent_a
Mark agent_a outputs as advisory, not authoritative
requires-engineering: add provenance checks between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Kestra explicitly touches cloud storage data, database data, messages, and notifications, while Mentat handles source code and model-provider API keys. If regulated or residency-bound data is placed into Kestra and then opened by Mentat, the pair can create retention or residency mismatches. The profiles do not prove a specific jurisdiction mismatch, so medium is the higher justified severity.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in Kestra-managed artifacts or logs
IF Mentat is used on the same regulated files
IF the model provider or storage region differs from the data residency requirement
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared workspaces
Use synthetic or redacted inputs
Verify retention settings before running either agent
Restrict Mentat to non-regulated source trees
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls
